notes:
Deal summary: late-stage procurement but lost to AWS managed endpoints. Customer evaluated Redwood Dedicated and Private  (wanted VPC isolation + KMS integration) but procurement/security opted for AWS-native offering.

Key quotes / call snippets:
- VP Eng (final call, 2026-01-08): "Given our existing committed spend and marketplace discounts, we have to go with the native AWS endpoint — simplifies billing and support."
- Head of Security: "We need an HSM attestation / FIPS profile that we couldn't validate within our timeline."

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-09-12: Initial inbound; product-fit call. Identified semantic-search + embeddings heavy workload.
- 2025-10-02: Demo: Redwood Dedicated perf & latency walkthrough (Jordan, Priya).
- 2025-10-20: POC kickoff (3-week sample index + embedding performance tests). Drive: proposal-cedarshore-2026.pdf.
- 2025-11-12: Security questionnaire returned (gap on HSM attestation flagged). Jira SEC-1290 opened.
- 2025-12-05: Cost modeling workshop vs AWS + GCP (Priya led). Procurement requested firm TCO at 500M tokens/month.
- 2026-01-07: Final procurement meeting with Finance + Procurement + Security. Fireflies ff_20260107_2398.
- 2026-01-10: Procurement decision: select AWS-managed endpoints (SageMaker/Marketplace pricing). Deal closed Lost.

Reasons lost / analysis:
- Hyperscaler advantage: single-vendor billing, committed spend discounts through marketplace, existing enterprise contract with AWS.
- Security: AWS provided immediate HSM/KMS attestation and PrivateLink architecture that satisfied their compliance team faster than our timeline.
- Procurement friction: Cedarshore has procurement policy favoring in-contract cloud vendors to reduce number of vendor relationships.
- No internal champion after Q4 org shuffle; engineering sponsor moved to new program.
- Pricing: AWS presented a bundled discount if they commit to 2-year committed spend (procurement couldn't justify multi-vendor capex).

Open follow-ups / next actions (for Redwood):
- Send post-mortem notes and competitive checklist to Jordan + Priya (action: Jordan).
- Ask for brief exit survey (1 pager) about key decision drivers — try to recover later if AWS underperforms.
- Add SEC-1290 summary to security playbook; evaluate HSM attestation options and timeline to close that gap.
- Flag account for renewal outreach in 9–12 months if customer re-evaluates model vendor strategy.

Other internal notes (shorthand):
- AE: good rapport but lost on procurement policy > tech.
- SE: POC showed latency + throughput met SLO; no obvious perf gaps.
- Pricing: we were competitive on unit cost but could not match marketplace bundled discounts.
- Risk: low near-term upside; classify as closed-lost, monitor for AWS hiccups.

Linked artifacts:
- Fireflies id ff_20260107_2398 (final decision call).
- Drive: sales proposal + security FAQ in linked_drive_docs.
- Jira: INF-4521 (POC infra ask), SEC-1290 (security attestation request).

Short-term owner notes:
- Jordan: follow up to send exit packet by 2026-01-20.
- Priya: capture POC metrics into internal benchmark repo (for sales play referencing hyperscaler comparisons).

Outcome: Closed-Lost — competing win: AWS (managed endpoints / marketplace).
